items.title: Brain Circuit Pruned to Make Wild Foxes Friendly
items.snippet: How did wild foxes become cuddly companions in just generations? Researchers examining Belyaev's famous Siberian silver foxes discovered that domesticated foxes have fewer estrogen receptor alpha neurons in the ventromedial hypothalamus—the brain's innate attack center.

items.title: Single-Dose Psilocybin Lacks Lasting Behavioral Effects
items.snippet: Does psilocybin produce lasting behavioral changes in mice? A multi-lab consortium discovered that while acute effects are reproducible, a single dose produces no lasting reductions in anxiety or depression-like behaviors 24 hours later.

items.title: Pulmonary Hypertension Triggers Cognitive Decline
items.snippet: Why do so many pulmonary hypertension patients experience brain fog and memory decline? Pitt and UPMC researchers discovered that the NCOA7-driven inflammatory cascade affecting the lungs also triggers microglial neuroinflammation and severs cerebellar-frontal circuits.

items.title: Hearing Loss Sharpens Peripheral Vision by Quieting Visual Cortex Neurons
items.snippet: Does losing your hearing improve your sight? A new study reveals that adult-onset hearing loss enhances peripheral visual clarity through an unexpected mechanism: dampening neural activity to make visual processing more efficient.

items.title: Male and Female Brains Process Junk Food Differently
items.snippet: How quickly does junk food alter the brain? A study reveals that just 24 hours on a high-fat diet reshapes feeding circuits in the lateral hypothalamus, using completely different synaptic mechanisms in males and females to modulate weight gain.
